findings.premise: vscode-plugin/src/chat/cli-adapter.ts maps CLI tool_use, tool_call and command items into tool-call and file-edit turn events as the turn runs, and a tool-call event carries its command — so whether a turn has acted is observable before it fails.
findings.evidence:
The gathered evidence supports the premise.
- **Codex items:** vscode-plugin/src/chat/cli-adapter.ts:749 handles codex items with `if (itemType === 'command_execution' || itemType === 'tool_call')`, so both item types reach the tool-call path.
- **File edits:** cli-adapter.ts:605 emits `{ kind: 'file-edit', turnId, path: input['file_path'] ... }` from claude tool_use input. cli-adapter.ts:747 emits one codex 'file-edit' per path.
- **Event types:** stream-events.ts:51 declares `readonly kind: 'file-edit';`, and 'tool-call' is a declared TurnEvent kind (stream-events.ts:192 and the 'tool-call' test fixtures).
- **Command on the event:** Passing tests confirm it: "claude: a Bash tool_use sets ToolCallEvent.command from input.command" and "claude: tool_use maps to tool-call (with mcp parse) and file-edit with a hunk diff". Test fixtures carry `{ kind: 'tool-call', ..., command: 'npm test' }` (chat-panel.test.ts:428).
- **As the turn runs:** The mapping is per-line inside mapLine, while the turn is running. chat-panel.ts:1351/1356 reacts to 'file-edit' and 'tool-result' events mid-turn, so the host can see that a turn has acted before it ends.

"claude: a command-less tool_use omits command" and "codex: a tool_call item without a command omits command (k2)" show that some tool-call events have no command. This does not undercut the premise: the tool-call or file-edit event itself is enough to show the turn acted.
findings.action: None needed; the evidence confirms the premise. Optional wording fix: say the tool-call event carries its command "when the tool has one", because command-less tools omit `command`.

proposedFix.rationale: The evidence confirms the premise. The only imprecision is that `command` is optional on ToolCallEvent. That does not change the design, because the event's presence alone shows the turn has acted.

findings.premise: Only the newest turn reports to the chat panel; a superseded turn keeps running its CLI out of sight while the new message waits behind the per-session lock.

(2) The new message waits behind the per-session lock: turn-lifecycle.ts:217 reads "lease = await deps.locks.acquire(s.id, {". The lock is per session id and is awaited. session-lock.test.ts:58-64 confirms that a second acquire on the same id waits (onWaiting) while a different id ('s2') does not. The defect's own LLD (docs/standalone/defect-vscode-plugin-src-chat-chat-E202610108ca7382b/S001/LLD.md:71) adds that the lease is released by the attached process's exit. So the new turn can't proceed until the old CLI process exits. The DEF of the target Epic cites the same anchor (DEF.md:193 [[c14]] turn-lifecycle.ts:217). (3) The superseded turn keeps running its CLI: line 244 goes on with "The previous turn's process is…". The read is cut off at that point, but the sentence is clearly about the old process not being stopped. That fits a turn whose reporting is silenced while it still holds the lease. One small gap: the rest of line 244 isn't in the evidence, so the literal wording "keeps running" isn't quoted. The meaning is clear from the generation-bump comment and the lease-release-on-process-exit design. The anchor in chat-panel.ts wasn't probed, but the premise doesn't depend on it.

findings.premise: Message images/file attachments already live in a plugin attachment store that clears old files on start-up, and messages reference them by path.

The gathered evidence supports the premise, though it comes from the design docs and build record of the earlier paste-images Story. None of it is a direct read of the source file.

S001/CR.md:26 then reviews `vscode-plugin/src/chat/attachment-store.ts:1`, which shows the file was built.
- **Old files are cleared on start-up.** LLD.md:112 says extension.ts "sweeps at start with the same keep set and age as the output sweep". It also says the store's onEvict removes a session's attachments.

body.title: Per-repo chat turn queue with outbox

summary.prose: Messages to the dev chat wait their turn in plain sight. Each repository runs one chat turn at a time, in the order messages were sent, across every chat and window open on it; each chat shows its waiting messages, their place in line, and what failed, with a way to cancel or resend. Short provider or start-up outages are retried by themselves, and nothing is ever run, or run again, without the user knowing.

body.problem: In the VS Code dev chat, a message the user sends while the assistant is still working on a previous turn appears to hang. The running turn stops showing anything in the panel, since only the newest turn reports to it and a superseded turn reports nothing more [[c8]], yet it keeps working out of sight, and the new message waits behind it for as long as it runs, up to ten minutes [[c9]], with nothing telling the user what is happening or how far back in line they are. Turns from different chats on the same repository can run at the same time and edit the same working tree, since the lock is taken per chat session [[c14]], while decisions handed over from the document review pane wait in an in-memory list that is dropped when the chat panel or its window closes [[c10]]. The user cannot see what is waiting, cannot take a waiting message back, and a turn that dies with its window or fails on a passing provider outage leaves the user to discover it and retype.

nonGoals.text: A queue or consumer in the daemon, or the daemon running the chat CLI
nonGoals.rationale: The user chose a clean separation: chat-turn queues are kept apart from the daemon's own queues, and moving the CLI into the daemon is a separate, larger change.

nonGoals.text: A queue per chat or per window
nonGoals.rationale: The user chose one queue per repository so that no two turns edit the same working tree at once.

nonGoals.text: Interrupting a running turn by sending a message (stop-and-send-now or newest-wins)
nonGoals.rationale: The user chose strict order; Stop remains the way to end a running turn.
Cancel and resend cover the need; reordering conflicts with strict order.

nonGoals.text: Running a message unattended or running a turn again by itself, other than the bounded retries of an infrastructure failure before the turn acted
nonGoals.rationale: A turn may have side effects; the user decides whether to resend.

nonGoals.text: A hand-made queue file format, a file per message, or a third-party queue library
nonGoals.rationale: The user chose the store built into the runtime; libraries found were immature, server-based or native.

nonGoals.text: Storing images or file attachments in the queue
nonGoals.rationale: They already live in the attachment store; a message refers to them by path.

nonGoals.text: One shared queue between windows whose extension hosts run on different machines or as different users (a local window and a Remote-SSH, WSL or container window on the same repository)
nonGoals.rationale: The store lives in the extension host's home directory; sharing across hosts would need a network service, which the user ruled out with the daemon queue.

assumptions.text: The plugin can rely on the built-in SQLite module once its minimum VS Code version is raised to a floor whose extension host exposes it without a flag. Checked on the installed VS Code 1.141 by running its Electron as Node (Electron 43, Node 24.21): node:sqlite loads and opens a database. The floor, and a plain message at start-up on a VS Code without it, are fixed by the design (k5).

Windows whose extension hosts run on the same machine as the same OS user, without an INSRC_DAEMON_ROOT override, share one ~/.insrc and so one queue per repository. A window whose extension host runs elsewhere (Remote-SSH, WSL, a container) has its own ~/.insrc there and its own queue (a non-goal).
A turn's CLI process can be found alive or gone from another window by its process id, as the current session lock already does.

Whether a turn has acted can be told from its event stream before it fails: cli-adapter.ts parses the CLIs' tool_use, tool_call and command items into tool-call and file-edit turn events as the turn runs, and a tool-call event carries its command. The chat keeps no failure classification today; the daemon's isTransientCliError (src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts:558) classifies transient CLI failures and is the starting point S004's design weighs, adding a CLI that cannot start and an unreachable network.

constraints.text: The plugin reaches the daemon only over IPC and never opens the daemon's LMDB or LanceDB stores (no plugin source imports them today); the chat queue is the plugin's own store, apart from ~/.insrc/graph.lmdb and the Lance tables.

Stakeholder targets fixed by the approved spec: one queue per repository, strict order, no interrupt; a lease taken over only after 10 minutes without a heartbeat and with the turn's process gone; infrastructure retries limited to 3 (10 s, 1 min, 5 min) and only before the turn acted; about 500 records per repository, finished ones removed first, an overflowing message refused with a note.
Plugin UI follows the VS Code theme only, in the chat panel's existing style.
The turn lifecycle stays free of the vscode module and is injected with its dependencies, as it is today.

The plugin's minimum VS Code version is raised to a verified version whose extension host has node:sqlite unflagged, and the plugin says plainly that the VS Code version is unsupported when the module cannot be loaded.

stories.title: Run one chat turn per repository at a time, in the order messages were sent
stories.userValue: The user can keep sending messages while the assistant works; each one waits its turn instead of hiding the running turn and hanging behind it, and no two chats edit the repository at once.

functionalRequirements.statement: Every message sent in any chat on a repository joins that repository's one queue, from every VS Code window on it.
A message is taken from the front of the queue only by the window its chat belongs to, which acknowledges it as taken before its turn starts; no message is ever taken twice.
Turns run one at a time per repository, in the order their messages were sent; the running turn keeps showing in its chat while later messages wait.
Stop ends the running turn and the next waiting message then runs; sending a message never stops or hides the running turn.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn is running in a chat on a repository
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user sends another message in the same chat
acceptanceCriteria.then: the running turn keeps showing its output, the new message waits, and it runs as soon as the running turn ends

acceptanceCriteria.given: two chats, in one window or in two windows, are open on the same repository
acceptanceCriteria.when: a message is sent in each while a turn runs in the first
acceptanceCriteria.then: the turns run one after another in the order the messages were sent, never at the same time

acceptanceCriteria.given: a message is at the front of the queue
acceptanceCriteria.when: two windows on the repository look for the next message at the same moment
acceptanceCriteria.then: only the window its chat belongs to takes it, the message is marked taken before its turn starts, and it runs exactly once

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn is running and messages are waiting
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user presses Stop
acceptanceCriteria.then: the running turn ends and the next waiting message runs

stories.title: See, cancel and resend waiting messages in the chat's outbox
stories.userValue: The user always knows what is waiting, where it is in line and what went wrong, and can take back or resend a message without retyping it.

functionalRequirements.statement: Each chat panel shows an outbox listing that chat's waiting, failed and undelivered messages with their place in line, and one line saying how many messages from other chats are ahead.
A message leaves the outbox for the transcript when it is taken from the queue.
A waiting message can be cancelled, and a failed or undelivered one dismissed or resent with one action.
The outbox is the same after a window reload or restart.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn is running and the user has sent two more messages in this chat while another chat has one message ahead of them
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user looks at the chat panel
acceptanceCriteria.then: the outbox lists the two messages with their places in line and says one message from another chat is ahead

acceptanceCriteria.given: a message is waiting in the outbox
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user cancels it
acceptanceCriteria.then: it leaves the outbox and the queue and is never run

acceptanceCriteria.given: a message has failed or could not be delivered
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user presses resend on it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the same message, with its attachments, joins the back of the queue

acceptanceCriteria.given: messages are waiting or failed in a chat
acceptanceCriteria.when: the window is reloaded
acceptanceCriteria.then: the chat's outbox shows the same messages in the same places

stories.title: Keep the queue moving when a window dies, and keep it bounded
stories.userValue: A closed or crashed window never blocks the repository for longer than the agreed time, nothing is run again behind the user's back, and the queue never grows without bound or loses a message silently.

functionalRequirements.statement: While a turn runs, its window shows it is alive; another window takes over the queue only after 10 minutes without that sign of life and once the turn's process is confirmed gone.
The message whose turn died with its window is marked failed with a resend and is never run again by itself; a turn whose process is still running after a reload is picked up again.
A message whose window is closed when it reaches the front is marked not delivered with a resend, and the queue moves on.
Finished messages are removed to keep the stored records per repository within the agreed bound; a message that cannot fit is refused with a note in the chat, never dropped.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn is running in window A and window B has messages waiting on the same repository
acceptanceCriteria.when: window A crashes and its turn's process ends
acceptanceCriteria.then: after 10 minutes the queue moves on in window B, and the crashed turn's message shows as failed with a resend when its chat is next shown

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn is running a long task
acceptanceCriteria.when: its window keeps working for more than 10 minutes
acceptanceCriteria.then: no other window takes over, and the turn runs to its end

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn is running when the window is reloaded and its process is still running
acceptanceCriteria.when: the window comes back
acceptanceCriteria.then: the chat shows the turn continuing and its message is not marked failed

acceptanceCriteria.given: a message from a chat whose window has since been closed reaches the front
acceptanceCriteria.when: the queue reaches it
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is marked not delivered with a resend and the next message runs

acceptanceCriteria.given: the repository's queue is at its bound with no finished messages left to remove
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user sends a message
acceptanceCriteria.then: the message is refused with a note in the chat saying why, and nothing already queued is lost

stories.title: Retry a turn that failed on a passing infrastructure problem before it acted
stories.userValue: A provider hiccup or a start-up failure fixes itself without the user retyping, while a turn that already did something is never repeated.

functionalRequirements.statement: A turn that fails because the CLI could not start, or because the provider was rate limited, overloaded or unreachable, or timed out, before it made any tool call, command or edit, is retried up to 3 times, waiting 10 seconds, 1 minute and 5 minutes.
While it waits to retry it keeps its place at the front, and its outbox row shows the attempt and the time left, with retry-now and cancel.
After the last attempt, or for any failure after the turn acted, a refusal or error from the model, Stop, or an authentication failure, the message is marked failed with the error and a resend.
A momentary conflict on the queue's own store is waited out; if it persists the message is refused with a note.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn fails with a provider overload before it made any tool call or edit
acceptanceCriteria.when: the failure is reported
acceptanceCriteria.then: the message waits 10 seconds at the front, its outbox row shows attempt 1 of 3 with the time left, and it is run again

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn edited a file and then failed on a network error
acceptanceCriteria.when: the failure is reported
acceptanceCriteria.then: the message is marked failed with the error and a resend, and it is not run again

acceptanceCriteria.given: a message has failed three retries
acceptanceCriteria.when: the third retry fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is marked failed with the error and a resend and the next message runs

acceptanceCriteria.given: a message is waiting to retry
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user presses retry now or cancel
acceptanceCriteria.then: it runs at once, or leaves the queue, accordingly

acceptanceCriteria.given: a turn fails because the provider rejected the user's credentials
acceptanceCriteria.when: the failure is reported
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is not retried and the chat says how to sign in again

stories.title: Send review-pane decisions through the same queue
stories.userValue: A decision sent from the document review pane is never lost and waits, visibly, by the same rules as a typed message; today such a decision waits in an in-memory list of the chat host that is dropped when the chat panel or its window closes.

functionalRequirements.statement: A decision sent from the review pane joins the repository's queue as a message of the chat it goes to, and shows in that chat's outbox like a typed message.
It survives a reload or the chat panel being closed, and runs when it reaches the front with the chat open.
The review pane's separate waiting list is removed.
Images and files attached to any waiting or failed message are kept until the message is finished, cancelled or dismissed.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a chat turn is running
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user approves a document in the review pane
acceptanceCriteria.then: the decision waits in the chat's outbox and runs when the turn ends

acceptanceCriteria.given: the chat panel is closed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the user sends a decision from the review pane
acceptanceCriteria.then: the chat opens, the decision is in its outbox, and it runs in order

acceptanceCriteria.given: a message with an attached image is waiting
acceptanceCriteria.when: the attachment store clears old files on start-up
acceptanceCriteria.then: the image is kept and goes with the message when it runs
